en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Cittalatā Grove in the Itthivimāna (Maiden’s Vimānas)
4. The Story of the Caṇḍālī’s Mansion “O Caṇḍālī,
worship the feet of the illustrious Gotama!”
Out of compassion for him alone,
the Seventh Sage stood still.
"Compose your mind with full confidence."
"O you who are like the Tathāgatas, the Arahants!
Quickly pay homage with palms joined;
your life is short."
Urged by the one of developed mind who bore his final body,
Caṇḍālī paid homage at his feet.
Of the illustrious Gotama.
A cow killed him as he stood with palms joined in reverence to a Caṇḍālī woman.
Paying homage to the Fully Awakened One,
who brings light into the darkness:
"To him whose taints are exhausted, who is free from dust, and who is unshakable..."
“Having approached you, who were sitting alone in seclusion in the forest, I,
having attained the power of a deva, pay homage to you, O hero of great majesty.”
“Golden-hued, radiant, and of great glory,
having ascended their celestial mansions which are manifoldly adorned,
they are surrounded by throngs of celestial nymphs.”
“Who are you, O auspicious goddess, that pays homage to me?
“I am a Caṇḍālī, O Blessed One,
sent by you, the Hero.”
Bowing at the feet of the Arhat Gotama, the illustrious one—
having thus paid homage to his feet, I...
Having been severed from birth as a Caṇḍāla,
I have been reborn in the Nandana grove in a celestial mansion auspicious on all sides.
Standing there, preceded by a hundred thousand nymphs,
I am the most distinguished and the best among them.
In beauty, fame, and long life;
having performed many good deeds,
they are clearly comprehending and mindful.
“The compassionate Sage in the world—
O Bhante, we have come to pay homage to him.
Having said this, the Caṇḍālī—
Grateful and mindful of what has been done for her,
having paid homage at the feet of the Arahant,
she vanished right there.
The fourth is the Caṇḍālī-vimāna.
